statement: For positive integer $m$, let $S(m)$ and $P(m)$ be its digit sum and digit product. Show that for each $n$, there exist positive integers $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ with $S(a_1) < \cdots < S(a_n)$ and $S(a_i) = P(a_{i+1})$ (with $a_{n+1} = a_1$).

Let $S = \{1, \ldots, 2014\}$. Each nonempty $T \subseteq S$ has a chosen representative. Find the number of ways so that if $D = A \cup B \cup C$ (disjoint), the representative of $D$ is also the representative of one of $A$, $B$, $C$.
Find all positive integers $n$ such that for any integer $k$, there exists an integer $a$ with $n \mid a^3 + a - k$.
$n$ is $b$-discerning if there exists a set of $n$ distinct positive integers $< b$ with no two subsets having equal sum. (a) Prove 8 is 100-discerning. (b) Prove 9 is not 100-discerning.

Circles $\omega$ and $\Omega$ meet at $A$ and $B$. $M$ is the midpoint of arc $AB$ on $\omega$ (inside $\Omega$). Chord $MP$ of $\omega$ meets $\Omega$ at $Q$ (inside $\omega$). Let $\ell_P$, $\ell_Q$ be tangents to $\omega$ at $P$ and $\Omega$ at $Q$. Prove the circumcircle of the triangle formed by $\ell_P$, $\ell_Q$, and $AB$ is tangent to $\Omega$.
